key_insight: The paper introduces a hardware-efficient variational ansatz whose binary-tree parametrization has an exact diagonal Fubini-Study metric, enabling efficient quantum natural gradient, time evolution, and Haar sampling without auxiliary metric circuits or matrix inversion.
engineering_relevance: This could substantially reduce two-qubit gate counts and simplify training for quantum chemistry, quench dynamics, and symmetry-respecting state preparation on near-term hardware.
method: Binary-tree parameterized ansatz with closed-form diagonal pullback metric
Pruning compiler converts gauge redundancy into linearly scaling circuits for sparse sector states
Interchangeable Schur-transform or reparameterization dressings enforce exact spin adaptation
evidence_signal: The abstract reports reference-level accuracy on small-molecule electronic structure and Hubbard quench benchmarks using one to three orders of magnitude fewer two-qubit gates than leading alternatives.
watch_item: The bare ansatz is classically simulable in the sector-sparse setting, so quantum advantage depends on adding a classically hard dressing and on practical control of compiler/pruning overheads.
paper_title: A hardware-efficient variational ansatz with an exact diagonal metric for real- and imaginary-time evolution and Haar sampling
